author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Microsoft plans to expand its global data-center capacity to about 38 gigawatts by 2032, more than triple its current footprint, Bloomberg News reported Thursday through people familiar with the plans.

The company now operates about 12 gigawatts of capacity, according to the report, but only about 2 gigawatts is dedicated to AI-specific chips. Roughly one-third of the planned 38-gigawatt total is expected to serve specialized AI hardware. Microsoft did not immediately respond to Reuters’ request for comment.

The scale reflects the computing and electricity demands of generative-AI products such as Copilot and ChatGPT. Microsoft has forecast $50 billion in capital spending for its fiscal first quarter of 2027 and $175 billion for calendar 2026.

Bloomberg also reported that Microsoft intends to spread some long-term data-center leases over 25 years instead of 15, reducing annual reported capital expenditures. The capacity target remains a reported plan rather than a company announcement, and bringing it online would require power agreements, construction, networking equipment and large supplies of advanced chips across multiple regions.
dek: Bloomberg reported a target of roughly 38 gigawatts, with about one-third expected to support AI-specific chips; Microsoft did not immediately comment.
headline: Microsoft plans to triple data-center capacity by 2032, report says
